best_for: C and C++ developers on Windows or Mac who build projects that ship a CMakeLists.txt and need a specific CMake version to match a project or CI setup.
description:
CMake is a family of open-source tools for building, testing and packaging software, from Kitware. Bill Hoffman, a Kitware co-founder and its CTO, first wrote it as a cross-platform build setup for the Insight Toolkit (ITK) and the Visualization Toolkit (VTK). Kitware says it now gets more than 2 million downloads a month.

You describe your project in plain configuration files, and one source tree can feed several builds, static or shared libraries, and deep folder layouts that depend on many libraries. It even handles programs that must be built first to generate code for the final app. If you need help, Kitware sells training, support and custom builds, and offers an on-demand CMake course.

points.title: It writes build files, it does not compile
points.text: CMake reads your project's configuration and generates native build files for the toolchain on each platform. Your compiler and build tool still do the actual work.

points.title: Free and BSD licensed
points.text: CMake is open source under the BSD 3-Clause license, with no paid edition.

points.title: Windows: MSI or zip, three architectures
points.text: Windows builds come as an MSI that installs for the whole machine, or a zip you can unpack anywhere without admin rights, each for x86, x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 92 versions.

points.title: Match the version a project expects
points.text: When a project or build server is set up for a particular CMake release, the 92 Windows builds here let you install that exact one instead of the newest.

points.title: Mac gets one universal build
points.text: macOS gets a universal disk image for Intel and Apple silicon on macOS 12 or later; cmake.org also offers a variant for macOS 10.10. Only the current Mac release is listed here, so older ones need cmake.org.

points.title: Linux is not listed here
points.text: Kitware publishes x86_64 and aarch64 Linux builds as a .sh installer or tar.gz on cmake.org, and most distributions package CMake, but this site does not track them.
